name: Odia, Bengali & Bihari Totke
summary: Pakhala, bel pana, sattu, thankuni and sorse tel from eastern India.

remedies.name: Pakhala Pani
remedies.howItHelps: Fermented rice water from Odisha keeps you cool and gives salts and good bacteria.
steps: Soak cooked rice in water overnight.
Drink the water with salt and a squeeze of lime.

remedies.name: Bel Pana
remedies.howItHelps: Wood-apple drink made for Pana Sankranti. Cools you down and its fiber helps the tummy.
steps: Scoop out bel pulp and soak it in water.
Mash, strain, and add a little jaggery.

remedies.name: Namkeen Sattu Ghol
remedies.howItHelps: Bihar's summer saviour: roasted gram in salted lemon water.
steps: Stir two spoons of sattu into cold water.
Add salt, roasted jeera and lemon.

remedies.name: Thankuni Pata Bata
remedies.howItHelps: Bengali grandmothers grind thankuni (Indian pennywort) leaves for upset tummies.
steps: Grind a few thankuni leaves with a pinch of salt.
Eat a little with the first bite of rice.

remedies.name: Warm Mustard Oil Massage
remedies.howItHelps: Gently warmed mustard oil with garlic is rubbed on legs and chest to warm and soothe.
steps: Grown-up warms mustard oil with a garlic clove.
Cool it till warm, then massage legs, soles and chest.
remedies.caution: Grown-up checks the oil isn't hot.

remedies.name: Tulsi Pata & Madhu
remedies.howItHelps: Tulsi juice with honey, a classic for coughs in Bengal and Odisha.
steps: Crush a few tulsi leaves to get juice.
Mix with a spoon of honey and lick slowly.
